Messages.Author: wijsman
Messages.Body:
Hello again,
I was wondering if the action by which an assamite can move one blood
from the blood bank to heartblood is at +1 stealth? Is this type of
action an undirected action, as described in the rule book? This rule
states :'There is one more complication: nondirected actions at +1
stealth are harder to block.' I say this rule can be interpreted two
ways: all nondirected actions are at +1 stealth, or more accent on the
'harder to block', so only those nondirected actions which are at +1
stealth are harder to block. Can anybody tell me which is the right
interpretation?

Thanks.

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
On Thu, 2 Dec 1999, wijsman wrote:

> Hello again,
> I was wondering if the action by which an assamite can move one blood
> from the blood bank to heartblood is at +1 stealth?

No. No stealth modifier is stated on the card, so it is at the default of
0 stealth. (The assamites have an easy time getting stealth with
Obfuscate anyway.)

--

James Coupe

Messages.Author: Sorrow
Messages.Body:
> I was wondering if the action by which an assamite can
> move one blood from the blood bank to heartblood is
> at +1 stealth?

If it doesn't say so on the card, then it is not. And since
it doesn't say so in this case, it isn't a +1 stealth action

> Is this type of action an undirected action, as described
> in the rule book?

Yes

> This rulestates :'There is one more complication: nondirected

> actions at +1 stealth are harder to block.'

I don't see this text in the revised rulebook. Which
are you looking at? If it isn't the revised rulebook,
my suggestion would be to get and read it.

> I say this rule can be interpreted two ways: all nondirected
> actions are at +1 stealth, or more accent on the 'harder to
> block', so only those nondirected actions which are at +1
> stealth are harder to block. Can anybody tell me which is
> the right interpretation?

It isn't.
Undirected actions are simply actions that are not directed
against another Meth or any cards under her control. Also,
all actions directed against yourself become undirected.
There are several basic action types as defined in the rule
book that are both undirected and at +1 stealth:
Hunting
Equipping
Recruiting an Ally/Retainer
Political Action

and as such are, as your rulebook quote says, harder to
block. Anything else will require specific card text indicating
that the action is at +1 stealth.

Sorrow

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
wijsman wrote:
>
> Hello again,

> I was wondering if the action by which an assamite can move one blood

> from the blood bank to heartblood is at +1 stealth? Is this type of

No. Minions have 0 stealth on their actions by deault: "By default, minions
have zero stealth and zero intercept. So a block attempt will normally succeed
unless the action has inherent stealth (such as hunting) or a card or effect is
used to increase the acting minion's stealth." [6.2.2.2]

> action an undirected action, as described in the rule book? This rule

Yes: "If the action is not directed at another Methuselah (or at something
controlled by another Methuselah), then the action is called undirected"
[6.2.2.1]

> states :'There is one more complication: nondirected actions at +1

> stealth are harder to block.' I say this rule can be interpreted two

That's a quote from an outdated rulebook. Try the revised rulebook (linked
in my .sig below).

> ways: all nondirected actions are at +1 stealth, or more accent on the

Not all nondirected actions are at +1 stealth, and not all actions at
+1 stealth are nondirected.

> 'harder to block', so only those nondirected actions which are at +1
> stealth are harder to block. Can anybody tell me which is the right
> interpretation?

It isn't "only" those nondirected actions which are at +1 stealth that
are harder to block - it is any action at +1 stealth. But it is true
that nondirected actions at +1 stealth are harder to block than nondirected
actions at no stealth.

--

Thats exactly what I thought when I read the post! Who wants to block my
Parnassus! Come on - any takers? Please? I would play with the Heartblood
card IF I thought you all would block my Assamites. :)

The Heartblood card has always been one that I would like to use in my
Assamite decks but it just could not make the final cut. The reasoning is
because it takes an action to move the a blood down to the Heartblood.
Normally in Assamite decks you need to use every action you can with none
being wasted so most of my actions are bleeds to oust my prey. The idea
that I have had in order to fully utilize the Heartblood would be to give
Parnassus Rutor's Hand do he could bleed and perform a Heartblood action
therefor not wasting any action. Just have not gotten around to it yet...

Another idea to get the Heartblood to work well is to create several smaller
babies and have them perform the Heartblood actions to bring out the
Assamite Elders. And if someone actually blocked the baby then you Mask of
1000 Faces and reveal that it was actually Abd al-Rashid, or Melek, or
Husamettin, etc. etc. Now THAT would be fun.

Just some random thoughts.
